entry.summary:
An incident response checklist for possible CVE-2026-113867 account abuse
An investigation into CVE-2026-113867 should begin with a version and configuration question, then move to account history only when the relevant XMPP path was present. The flaw could inject outbound stanzas through Thunderbird, but the reviewed sources do not show a universal compromise marker. A disciplined timeline can separate vulnerable systems from confirmed abuse. Mozilla documented CVE-2026-113867 in MFSA 2026-114 and MFSA 2026-115. Thunderbird did not escape attribute values when serializing outgoing XMPP stanzas. entry.title: Migrating Secrets Management: AWS Parameter Store vs Azure Key Vault
entry.summary:
Why Secrets Management Is the First Thing You’ll Hit When Switching Clouds
When you move an application from Amazon Web Services to Microsoft Azure, the first thing that usually breaks isn’t the compute layer—it’s the way you keep passwords, API keys, and certificates safe. In AWS many teams rely on AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store (or the older AWS Secrets Manager) to fetch values at runtime. Azure’s counterpart is Azure Key Vault. Both services provide encryption‑at‑rest, fine‑grained IAM, and versioning, but their SDKs, authentication flows, and naming conventions differ enough that a naïve copy‑paste will throw a ResourceNotFound or an authentication error. entry.title: SQL in Depth: Interactive WASM SQLite 3 Workbench & Database Internals from First Principles
entry.summary:
Most SQL tutorials stop at syntax (JOIN, GROUP BY, window functions) and leave you guessing when a real production query suddenly slows down. Understanding why a query is slow means understanding how the database engine actually parses, plans, indexes, and executes it. Passive reading about B-Trees, query plans, and transaction isolation only gets you so far—it clicks much faster when you can run queries and watch the internals step by step. That's why I built SQL in Depth, a free, open-source interactive textbook covering SQL and database internals from first principles. Everything runs right in the browser with no accounts, no paywalls, and no local DB setup. Try it live: sql-in-depth.vedgupta.in
Source code on GitHub: github.com/innovatorved/sql-in-depth
What's Inside
Interactive WASM SQLite 3 Workbench — write and run real SQLite 3 queries directly in the browser alongside each lesson. Table-Level Relational Visualizer — watch how joins, filters, groupings, and transformations operate on actual rows step by step. 180 Structured Units — from relational algebra and core SQL semantics to indexing, query optimization, storage internals, and transactions. 36 Interactive Simulators — experiment hands-on with database internals and see how design trade-offs behave. If you're preparing for backend interviews, sharpening your SQL fundamentals, or curious about how relational engines work under the hood, give it a spin! If you find it useful, a star on GitHub helps others discover it—and issues, PRs, or ideas for new simulators are always welcome in the comments or on GitHub.

entry.summary: Most “open data” about places is heavier than you need.
